findings.text: D1-RERUN-CHANCE states 6 of the 12 BASE/RAW readers died after the write and before the hand-back; transcripts show 4 (RAW-A_2, RAW-B_0, RAW-B_1, RAW-B_2) ending in an API-error block after a valid sealed write with no hand-back call; the other 8 handed back DONE. Count correction only; answers unaffected.
The hand-back is not required by the audit function; the 4 readers without it are VALID and their answer files equal their heredocs. RAW-A_2 emitted a plain-text DONE before the error.

BASE-A_0 and BASE-A_2 each emitted one 50-character assistant text block (no braces, no Greek) before their first tool call, i.e. before any image was read; not a tool call and cannot carry answer content.

Model-stage brief files end with a newline that the delivered prompt lacks, so the prompt sha256 differs from the recorded brief_sha256 for the 18 model agents and 6 dead agents; content is otherwise identical (J-seal and REF briefs have no trailing newline and match exactly).

J-seal material paths carry set/kind folder names: the blank picker's 2 images lie under /work/jseal/blank/ and the sealers' 5 under /work/jseal/J/. This predates DECL-D1-A5 item 2 (declared 05:59:34Z, applying to D1 reader images; picker launched 05:54:08Z). The folder name could bias blank confirmation toward 'no writing'; the D1 blank bar rests on reader namings, not the picker's.
src/hercules/harness/jobs.py (brief header generator) appears in no METRIC-HASH record; every D1 brief header was re-derived exactly from its current HEADER and the job record, so there is no effect.

/srv/scorer key and item-map files were not opened by this auditor (permission denied); freshness and image kinds were established from job-list membership and transcript reads, not from the display key.
